questions.stem: Which Indian became the FIRST to win the prestigious Miss World title on the international stage?

options.option_text: Aishwarya Rai, who won the Miss World title in 1994
Reita Faria, who won the Miss World crown in 1966
Priyanka Chopra, the Miss World titleholder of 2000
Diana Hayden, representing India at Miss World in 1997

questions.explanation: Reita Faria (1966) was the first Indian to win Miss World, nearly three decades before Aishwarya Rai (1994). The most tempting wrong answer is Aishwarya Rai because she is far more famous, but she was actually the fourth Indian to win the title.

questions.stem: Who was the FIRST woman to serve as the Governor of an Indian state after Independence?

options.option_text: Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit, India's first woman UN Assembly President
Sarojini Naidu, appointed Governor of United Provinces in 1947
Padmaja Naidu, who later served as Governor of West Bengal
Sucheta Kriplani, the first woman Chief Minister of India

questions.explanation: Sarojini Naidu was appointed Governor of United Provinces (now Uttar Pradesh) in August 1947, making her India's first woman Governor. A common trap is Padmaja Naidu (her daughter), who served as Governor of West Bengal but from 1956 onward. Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit was India's first woman ambassador, not Governor.

questions.stem: Abhinav Bindra won India's first individual Olympic gold medal in 2008. Before him, all of India's Olympic gold medals had come exclusively in which team sport?

options.option_text: Badminton, with multiple gold medals in the Thomas Cup team event
Field Hockey, with India winning 8 gold medals between 1928 and 1980
Cricket, which appeared briefly in the 1900 Paris Olympics program
Football, with India qualifying for the team event at 1948 London

questions.explanation: India's 8 Olympic gold medals in field hockey (1928–1980) were all team golds — not individual. The Thomas Cup is a badminton world team championship, not an Olympic competition, making option A a deliberate trap. Cricket appeared in the 1900 Olympics, but India was not a participant in that edition.

questions.stem: Which became India's FIRST state to be carved out on purely linguistic lines, predating the States Reorganisation Act of 1956?

options.option_text: Karnataka, formed by merging Kannada-speaking regions of South India
Andhra State, separated from Madras State in October 1953
Maharashtra, created after the Samyukta Maharashtra Andolan agitation
Kerala, formed by merging Travancore-Cochin with Malabar district

questions.explanation: Andhra State was created on October 1, 1953, from Telugu-speaking districts of Madras State, following Potti Sriramulu's 58-day fast-unto-death. Karnataka, Maharashtra, and Kerala were all created in 1956 under the States Reorganisation Act, three years after Andhra State's formation.

questions.stem: The inaugural Dadasaheb Phalke Award — India's highest honour in cinema — was conferred in 1969. Who was its first recipient?

options.option_text: Prithviraj Kapoor, patriarch of the illustrious Kapoor film dynasty
Lata Mangeshkar, the legendary playback singer of Hindi film industry
Devika Rani, celebrated as the 'First Lady of Indian Cinema'
Pankaj Mullick, the celebrated Bengali vocalist and music composer

questions.explanation: Devika Rani received the inaugural Dadasaheb Phalke Award in 1969. A pioneering actress of early Indian cinema and grand-niece of Rabindranath Tagore, she was a natural choice for the first award. Prithviraj Kapoor is the most tempting wrong answer — he received it in 1971, not the first year. Lata Mangeshkar received it in 1989.

questions.stem: India's FIRST product to receive a Geographical Indication (GI) registration under the GI of Goods (Registration & Protection) Act, 1999 was:

options.option_text: Kanchipuram Silk, the sacred weave from Tamil Nadu's temple towns
Darjeeling Tea, registered as GI Application No. 1 in the year 2004
Basmati Rice, grown across the Indo-Gangetic plains of North India
Mysore Silk, produced by the Karnataka Silk Industries Corporation

questions.explanation: Darjeeling Tea was granted India's first GI registration as Application No. 1 in 2004. Basmati Rice is the most tempting wrong answer because it is globally synonymous with Indian agriculture, but it does not hold a GI tag under this Act. Kanchipuram Silk and Mysore Silk are legitimate GI products but received their registrations after Darjeeling Tea.

questions.stem: Who became the FIRST woman to be elected President of the Indian National Congress, holding that position nearly a decade before the first Indian woman was similarly honoured?

options.option_text: Sarojini Naidu, who became INC president at the 1925 Kanpur session
Nellie Sengupta, British-born leader who chaired the INC session in 1933
Annie Besant, Theosophist leader who presided over the INC in 1917
Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit, diplomat and the sister of Jawaharlal Nehru

questions.explanation: Annie Besant (British Theosophist) became the first woman President of INC at the 1917 Calcutta session. Sarojini Naidu (1925, Kanpur) was the first INDIAN woman to hold the position — which the stem hints at by saying 'nearly a decade later.' Nellie Sengupta is an expert-level distractor since she was also a British woman who chaired the INC, but in 1933, not 1917. Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit never served as INC president.
